extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: HELVIPAD is a real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 39,553 labeled video frames from 29 sequences captured in diverse indoor and outdoor environments under various lighting conditions. Data were collected using two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup paired with a LiDAR sensor, providing depth and disparity labels via projection of 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images. An augmented training set with increased label density via depth completion is also included.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene (EPFL); Jannik Endres (EPFL, TU Darmstadt); Albias Havolli (EPFL); Charles Corbière (EPFL); Salim Cherkaoui (EPFL); Alexandre Kontouli (EPFL); Alexandre Alahi (EPFL)
extraction.citeAs: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi. HELVIPAD: A Real-World Dataset for Omnidirectional Stereo Depth Estimation. arXiv:2411.18335, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a synchronized Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor, mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis. The rig was driven through indoor and outdoor scenes on a university campus, capturing equirectangular images at 30 fps and LiDAR point clouds at 10 fps across 29 video sequences in diverse environments including corridors, halls, pedestrian squares, footpaths, roads, and parking areas under various lighting and weather conditions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The LiDAR sensor has a vertical field of view of only 42.4°, meaning depth labels from LiDAR point clouds cover only a fraction of total pixels (approximately 12% of pixels before depth completion). Additionally, the depth completion approach is limited for fast-moving objects like cars, as temporal aggregation over a limited window may introduce errors for such objects. Sky areas and regions lacking nearby LiDAR measurements are excluded from depth labeling.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw equirectangular video frames from two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras (initial resolution 3840×1920 pixels at 30 fps) and 3D point clouds from an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor (64 beams, 42.4° vertical field of view, operating at 10 fps), captured across 29 video sequences on a university campus.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Dataset is collected on a single university campus, which may underrepresent other environments; outdoor night sequences are underrepresented compared to daytime sequences; depth completion increases density of low-range depth values (0–10 meter range), enriching representation of closer objects relative to farther ones
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Depth completion temporal aggregation is limited for fast-moving objects like cars; the dataset was collected on a university campus, which may limit generalization to other environments; indoor-trained models show a clear limitation in generalizing to outdoor scenes, particularly at night; the depth completion pipeline does not provide labels for pixels at object boundaries; occlusions between LiDAR and cameras were not explicitly handled
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is collected in dynamic human environments including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes, featuring pedestrians. It is intended to support mobile robot navigation and interaction in real-world human environments, including healthcare and autonomous driving applications.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset was collected in public and semi-public spaces on a university campus and includes video frames of human pedestrians in dynamic scenes. No explicit statement is made about anonymization or redaction of individuals captured in the imagery.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Developing and benchmarking omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models capable of navigating in human environments; assessing the robustness of depth estimation methods to diverse lighting conditions and depth ranges; training and evaluation of stereo depth estimation models for robotic navigation and exploration in complex indoor environments
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: An augmented training set was created using a depth completion pipeline tailored for 360° images. The pipeline performs temporal aggregation of LiDAR point clouds (fusing the current frame with four preceding and four succeeding frames), interpolates depth on spherical grid points using a weighted k-nearest-neighbor average, and filters out points with high uncertainty or insufficient nearby measurements. This increases the ratio of labeled pixels from 12% to 61% and is used as a data augmentation technique for training stereo depth estimation models.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Raw equirectangular images were captured at 3840×1920 pixels and downsampled to a width of 512 pixels. Top images, bottom images, depth maps, and disparity maps were cropped to remove unnecessary borders (sky, ground). Camera frames were subsampled from 30 fps to 10 fps to match the LiDAR frame rate. LiDAR point clouds were projected onto equirectangular images via an optimized rotation and translation transformation (minimizing reprojection error using BFGS). Depth values were converted to spherical disparity in degrees. Synchronization between sensors was achieved using a hardware flash trigger, with data streams re-aligned to a common reference timestamp. The final dataset comprises 39,553 paired images at 1920×512 pixels resolution.
